predecessors.name: Hittite Empire
predecessors.text: Kammanu on 'a plateau (Malatya Plain), north of the Taurus Mountains and west of the Euphrates', capital Melid; the province (11,100 km2) is the researcher's reading

successors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
successors.text: Kammanu without the city of Melid: the Malatya Plain 'annexed by Assyria' in 712 (Malatya Province minus the Melid cell, about 10,900 km2, the researcher's reading)

successors.name: Kummuh
successors.text: the city of Melid (Melitene, Arslantepe, east of modern Malatya) 'placed under the rule of Mutallu, king of Kummuh' in 712 BCE after Sargon II dismembered Melid; one gazetteer cell (about 250 km2)…

ledger.x: c. 1200 BC: Kammanu forms. 'Formed from part of Kizzuwatna after the Hittite Empire collapsed', 'around 1200 BCE'; the Melid page has the city 'the center of an independent Luwian Neo-Hittite state of Kammanu' from the 12th to the 7th century.
719 BC: Assyria deposes Gunzinanu and sets up a vassal.
712 BC: Kammanu is annexed by Assyria.
712 BC: the city of Melid is handed to Kummuh.
712 BC: the Neo-Hittite kingdom of Kammanu ends; at the same time Cimmerians and Scythians invaded Anatolia and the city declined.

wars.name: Sargon II's conquest of Melid
wars.outcome: Sargon II sacked Melid in 712 BC; Tarhunazi was deposed after a failed rebellion, Kammanu was annexed by Assyria and the city of Melid was placed under Mutallu of Kummuh.

certainty.note: The page describes a plateau but no frontier or area; the shape is the modern province.
